log.text: Aurora Veil up on P2's side

decisions.rationale: Pelipper sets Drizzle, Swampert Mega Evolves and threatens physical offense alongside backline Basculegion and Archaludon.
decisions.notebook: Opponent roster: Whimsicott, Gholdengo, Blastoise, Maushold, Ninetales-Alola, Tauros-Paldea-Blaze. Whimsicott denies rain with Sunny Day; Gholdengo blocks status; Blastoise mega evolves.

decisions.rationale: Lead Whimsicott + Gholdengo to overwrite rain immediately with Prankster Sunny Day while applying strong spread Steel pressure. Ninetales-Alola provides a second weather option, Aurora Veil, and Freeze-Dry pressure on the rain core. Tauros benefits greatly from sun, gives Intimidate support, and pressures Swampert and Archaludon physically.
decisions.notebook: Opponent rain mode centers on Damp Rock Pelipper and may use Tailwind, Rain Dance, or Wide Guard. Mega Swampert is an Adamant physical attacker with Waterfall, Ice Punch, Earthquake, and Protect; preserve Gholdengo from Ground pressure. Choice Scarf Adaptability Basculegion threatens immediate Water/Ghost damage and Last Respects. Archaludon may use Electro Shot or Iron Defense, so deny setup and pressure it quickly. Sunny Day is a key rain-reversal tool; Ninetales-Alola offers additional weather control and Aurora Veil.

decisions.rationale: Pelipper sets Tailwind to outspeed after Whimsicott's Prankster Sunny Day, and Swampert Mega Evolves and uses Waterfall on Whimsicott to pressure/break Focus Sash while threatening Gholdengo next.
Bring in Basculegion to outspeed and pressure with Choice Scarf (Wave Crash/Last Respects), and use Swampert-Mega's Earthquake to hit Gholdengo super-effectively while Whimsicott is present.
decisions.notebook: Opponent roster: Whimsicott, Gholdengo, Blastoise, Maushold, Ninetales-Alola, Tauros-Paldea-Blaze. Whimsicott Prankster Sunny Day denies rain; Gholdengo Good as Gold blocks status. Scarf Basculegion outspeeds Whimsicott and the rest of the team.

selection: Sunny Day (all adjacent, including ally Gholdengo)
decisions.rationale: Use priority Sunny Day to reverse rain before attacks, weakening Water pressure and preventing Mega Swampert’s Swift Swim boost. Gholdengo’s Thunderbolt then reliably OHKOs Pelipper through its 4× weakness, removing Tailwind, Wide Guard, and rain control.
decisions.notebook: Pelipper is a central rain-control piece with Damp Rock and may use Tailwind, Rain Dance, or Wide Guard; Thunderbolt from exact Modest Gholdengo reliably OHKOs it. Sunny Day is valuable for reversing rain and denying Mega Swampert’s Swift Swim advantage. Preserve Gholdengo from Ground pressure; Mega Swampert’s Earthquake remains its key threat. Scarf Adaptability Basculegion threatens immediate Water/Ghost damage, while Archaludon can use Electro Shot or Iron Defense. Ninetales-Alola provides a secondary weather-control and Aurora Veil option.

decisions.rationale: Scarf Basculegion outspeeds Whimsicott and Gholdengo, so Last Respects on Gholdengo KO's or heavily chips it before Gholdengo moves. Swampert Mega Earthquake hits both foes (super-effective on Gholdengo).
decisions.notebook: Scarf Basculegion outspeeds the entire opponent roster. Keep track of fainted Pelipper for Last Respects power.

decisions.rationale: Encore locks Mega Swampert into its previously used Waterfall, preventing the spread Earthquake threat to Gholdengo. Gholdengo then uses super-effective Shadow Ball into Basculegion, preserving pressure while Whimsicott’s priority action protects the team from the most dangerous board swing.
decisions.notebook: Pelipper’s rain-control role was successfully removed in game 2; Sunny Day remains valuable against future rain attempts. Preserve Gholdengo from Ground pressure, especially Mega Swampert Earthquake. Scarf Adaptability Basculegion remains an immediate Ghost/Water threat. Ninetales-Alola offers backup weather control and Aurora Veil; Tauros-Paldea-Blaze offers Intimidate and offensive pressure.

decisions.rationale: Keep Whimsicott active to exploit Encore on Mega Swampert’s Waterfall. Bring in Tauros-Blaze for Intimidate against both physical attackers, preserve Sunny Day, and add immediate offensive pressure; Ninetales would overwrite the sun and provide less immediate value.
decisions.notebook: Pelipper’s rain-control role was successfully removed in game 2. Sunny Day remains a valuable response to future rain attempts. Preserve Gholdengo from Ground pressure when possible, especially Mega Swampert Earthquake. Scarf Adaptability Basculegion is an immediate Ghost/Water threat. Ninetales-Alola provides backup weather control and Aurora Veil; Tauros-Paldea-Blaze provides Intimidate and offensive pressure.

decisions.rationale: Basculegion outspeeds and picks off Whimsicott with Last Respects. Swampert is encored into Waterfall, so switching Swampert to Archaludon removes the Encore lock, preserves momentum, and brings in a powerful Stamina/Electro Shot threat under the sun.
decisions.notebook: Scarf Basculegion outspeeds the entire opponent roster. Keep track of fainted Pelipper for Last Respects power. Swampert was encored into Waterfall on turn 2 and switched out on turn 3 to clear the encore.

decisions.rationale: Whimsicott uses Prankster Tailwind to secure future speed control and let Tauros pressure before the Scarfed Basculegion. Tauros Protects this turn, avoiding both Basculegion’s locked Last Respects and Swampert’s locked Waterfall while preserving both attackers for the next turn.
decisions.notebook: Pelipper has been removed in game 2, reducing the opponent’s demonstrated rain-control options. Preserve Sunny Day as a response to future rain attempts. Scarf Adaptability Basculegion remains a major Ghost/Water threat; protect or exploit its Choice lock when possible. Mega Swampert’s demonstrated Encore/Waterfall lock can be used for positioning. Preserve Gholdengo from Ground pressure in future games, especially Mega Swampert Earthquake. Ninetales-Alola remains backup weather control and Aurora Veil support; Tauros provides Intimidate and offensive pressure.

decisions.rationale: Whimsicott is at 7% HP and outspeeds under Tailwind, so Basculegion KOes Whimsicott with Last Respects. Archaludon switches to Swampert-Mega to pivot into a favorable matchup against Tauros while preserving board position.
decisions.notebook: Scarf Basculegion outspeeds the entire opponent roster. Keep track of fainted Pelipper for Last Respects power.

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Switch Whimsicott to preserve it from the locked Last Respects; Ninetales can survive the hit and restore weather later if needed. Tauros uses Close Combat on Archaludon for the strongest immediate pressure and a possible KO, despite Stamina.
decisions.notebook: Pelipper is removed in game 2, reducing demonstrated rain control. Preserve Sunny Day against future rain attempts. Scarf Adaptability Basculegion is a major Ghost/Water threat; exploit its Last Respects lock or protect against it. Mega Swampert has demonstrated Encore/Waterfall lock and Earthquake pressure; preserve Gholdengo from Ground moves. Ninetales-Alola remains backup weather control and Aurora Veil support. Tauros provides Intimidate and offensive pressure.

decisions.rationale: Under Tailwind, Ninetales and Tauros move first. Ninetales is at 32% HP and threatened by Last Respects, while Swampert uses Earthquake to hit both opponents (Tauros takes 2x super-effective). Swampert is encored into Waterfall, so it must use Protect to stall out Encore while Basculegion attacks.
decisions.notebook: Basculegion Choice Scarf outspeeds everything; Swampert Mega is locked into Waterfall by Encore this turn. Keep track of Last Respects power.

selection: Aurora Veil (your side, including ally Tauros-Paldea-Blaze)
decisions.rationale: Aurora Veil reduces the incoming physical pressure while preserving both attackers. Tauros uses Close Combat on Swampert; combined with a later Freeze-Dry, this threatens the main remaining bulky attacker. Veil also improves Tauros’s chance to survive Waterfall and reduces Basculegion’s locked Last Respects damage.
decisions.notebook: Scarf Adaptability Basculegion is a major Ghost/Water threat; when locked into Last Respects, use protection, defensive support, or exploit its predictable targeting. Pelipper is removed in game 2, so future rain control is less demonstrated, but preserve Sunny Day and Ninetales weather control against rain attempts. Mega Swampert has shown Waterfall and Encore pressure; avoid exposing Gholdengo to Ground moves. Tauros provides Intimidate and offensive pressure, while Ninetales can provide Aurora Veil support.

decisions.rationale: Ninetales is fainted and must be replaced; Whimsicott is the only available Pokémon. Slot 2 has no remaining legal replacement, so it passes while Whimsicott enters slot 1.
decisions.notebook: Scarf Adaptability Basculegion is a major threat; when locked into Last Respects, prioritize protection, defensive support, or exploiting its predictable targeting. Preserve Sunny Day and Ninetales weather control against rain attempts. Tauros offers Intimidate and offensive pressure; Whimsicott provides speed control and support.

decisions.rationale: Basculegion uses Last Respects to KO Whimsicott (7% HP). Swampert-Mega is encored into Waterfall, so it attacks Whimsicott with Waterfall to ensure the win.
decisions.notebook: Basculegion Scarf outspeeds. Last Respects deals heavy damage. Swampert Mega locked into Waterfall by Encore.

decisions.rationale: Moonblast is the only damaging option and targets the larger immediate threat, chipping the Choice-locked Basculegion before it can use Last Respects again. Encore on Basculegion is redundant, while Encore on Swampert cannot stop Basculegion from attacking. Tailwind and Sunny Day do not preserve Whimsicott or improve this line enough.

reflections.summary: Basculegion's Choice Scarf outsped and cleaned up with Last Respects after Mega Swampert pressured the early game, overcoming the opponent's Tailwind and Aurora Veil setup.
reflections.adjustment: Retain the same team architecture but ensure Mega Swampert avoids predictable Encore vulnerabilities against Whimsicott leads.
reflections.notebook: Opponent brings Whimsicott, Gholdengo, Tauros-Paldea-Blaze, and Ninetales-Alola with Light Clay/Aurora Veil and Prankster Tailwind/Encore support. Basculegion Scarf outspeeds and leverages Last Respects.

reflections.summary: Lost because the chosen four had no reliable defensive answer to Scarf Adaptability Basculegion once Gholdengo fell; repeated Last Respects pressure overwhelmed the team despite Sunny Day, Tailwind, and Aurora Veil. The preview plan also lacked a Mega-capable counter to Mega Swampert, leaving Tauros and Ninetales poorly positioned for the endgame.
reflections.adjustment: Change the four to include a sturdier Basculegion/Mega Swampert answer, and if available bring and evolve a suitable Mega holder rather than accepting a non-Mega lineup. Preserve Gholdengo or another protected target so Basculegion cannot freely accumulate and fire off Last Respects.
reflections.notebook: Opponent commonly pairs rain lead Pelipper with Mega Swampert, then uses Scarf Adaptability Basculegion as a high-priority cleanup threat. Basculegion revealed repeated Last Respects pressure and can be locked into it; defensive protection, safe switching, and denying its free targets are priorities. Mega Swampert threatens the endgame with Waterfall and Earthquake, so future selections need a sturdier answer and should not rely solely on weather control or Intimidate.
